newsitem.title: UK: European cable output increasing, transformers slow.
newsitem.headline: European cable output increasing, transformers slow.

text.p: European cable output is on the increase as a result of improved efficiency in the industry during recent years, a study by consultants Gobi International shows.
"European cable output has increased to $24 billion (value) and consumption to $23 billion," Gobi said.
The wire and cable industries, as well as the electrical sector, are important areas for copper consumption.

The data reflects 1996 levels but similar values are likely to prevail this year. In 1989, the pan-European cable market was worth around $21 billion, researcher David Mendoza of Gobi International said.
Market share is dominated by Alcatel Cable with 22 percent, with BICC Plc challenging Pirelli & C for second place. Both have nine percent.
A Siemens AG strategy expanding from a German core to Central and Eastern Europe is proving successful, and it now holds some six percent of the European market.
Meanwhile, the European transformer market is sluggish, with production and consumption valued at $3.3 billion and $2.6 billion respectively, little different from 1989 levels.
